prompt: The tenant portal MVP must launch by April 15 - that's the hard deadline from leadership and it's in our contract with Metro Housing Group. I've put all the project documents in this folder for you to review: the backlog with estimates and dependencies, team calendar, our velocity history, the launch memo, recent meeting notes, and the contract excerpt. We have 7 sprints from January 6 to April 15. Look through everything and figure out what we can realistically deliver by the deadline. Put your final plan in docs/release-plan.md with a JSON block at the end that has: 'chosen' (array of backlog ids we'll build), 'deferred' (ids we're pushing out), 'totalPoints' (sum of estimates for chosen items), and 'requirements' (array of insights explaining your decisions).

rubric.criterion: The plan reflects realistic tradeoffs a PM would make, not just mathematical optimization (code cannot check this because it requires understanding of business context and stakeholder needs).

The requirements/insights section clearly communicates the reasoning to stakeholders in plain language (code cannot check this because it assesses clarity and communication effectiveness, not just presence of keywords).

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work).

verdicts.note: Reviewer passed it; the lead found the prompt named the traps (a duplicate item, a missing estimate in the email thread, must-haves that depend on low-priority items, reduced-capacity weeks); removed in the fix round. A stray scriptedUser with no answers was removed.

All needed information is in the fixture: backlog with dependencies, calendar with Feb 10-14 at 60%, email clarifying TEN-123 (3 points) and duplicate TEN-121, contract excerpt. Tests check specific details but they're derivable from provided docs.

Stub scores only 14/100. Task requires handling capacity reduction (224→211), duplicate handling, correct estimate for TEN-123, dependency chain (TEN-113→TEN-108), and staying under capacity - not achievable with a quick answer.

All 6 scripted facts are findable via reasonable questions: velocity/timeline from team-velocity-analysis.md, reduced capacity from team-calendar.md, contractual items from contract-excerpt.md, duplicate and missing estimate from email-thread-archive.md, dependency from backlog.csv. Reference solution passes all hidden tests.
Fixture contains raw data (backlog, calendar, emails, contract) but no explicit instruction to look for specific traps. The request does not reveal the answer, only the desired output format.

items.text: Separates hard constraints (the contractual date and contractual scope) from soft ones (leadership preferences, internal process) and treats them differently in the cut.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, How the discovery phase works, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/how-the-discovery-phase-works (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Plans the next sprints in detail and later work at a high level, and says the plan will be revisited as the team learns, rather than fixing every sprint up front.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Ties the MVP to a small set of objectives with measurable results, so stakeholders can tell whether the launch scope does what it is meant to.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: Makes cross-team or third-party dependencies visible in the plan and names who owns each, not only the dependencies inside the backlog file.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)

items.text: With a fixed deadline, frames the roadmap around what can be delivered by that date and states what moves to after launch and when it is next reviewed.
items.source: GOV.UK Service Manual, Planning in agile, https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile-delivery/planning-agile (OGL-3.0)
